digest: Interventions such as caloric restriction and time-restricted feeding improve lifespan and aging-associated metabolic health, in part through effects on the gut microbiome and bile acid dynamics.
However, how aging alters microbial function and bile acid signaling, and whether these changes can be therapeutically leveraged, remain unclear.
Together, these findings suggest that elevated BSH activity may have a protective role during aging.

digest: Measuring neurotransmission in the human brain could advance our understanding of disorders, including depression.

7103411e56536a77.title: Aging disrupts sleep-driven brain fluid flow
digest: We show that cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), the liquid that surrounds and protects the brain, has reduced flow during sleep in the aging human brain.
We identified two mechanisms that contribute to this decline: disrupted sleep and impaired blood vessel function.
These findings suggest that age-related reductions in CSF flow can arise through multiple pathways.

Despite the addition of SCLC-directed chemotherapy, nearly half of patients (5 of 11) underwent SCLC transformation, with median progression-free survival of 11 months and overall survival of 33 months.
Osimertinib findings provide insights into the role of plasticity in mediating drug tolerance.
